note: Read first 2026-11-03 in the University of Minnesota Human Rights Library's copies of the laws, each naming the issue of the Official Gazette it reproduces, since the State's laws database at the National Information Centre (yemen-nic.info) didn't answer without its www; read again the same day in that database (www.yemen-nic.info), where the Child Rights Law, art. 59, gives the age of majority in the same words as the Civil Law's art. 50, so fifteen stands on the State's own text; the Minnesota copies are no longer cited. Majority: 15. The Civil Law (Republican Decree-Law No. 14 of 2002, Official Gazette issue 7/1 of 2002), art. 50: the age of majority (سن الرشد) is fifteen full years; a person who reaches it of sound mind and prudent in their dealings has full capacity to exercise and dispose of their civil rights, and special laws may require a higher age (none held). Work: null here; the person research's working age (fifteen, under Ministerial Decision No. 11 of 2013 as WageIndicator summarises it, research/sources/person/ages/YE.json) and its reading that no exception lets a younger performer work are read from that file (tools/papers/ages/person.ts). The Child Rights Law (No. 45 of 2002, Official Gazette issue 22 of 2002), art. 133, read the same day, bars all work under fourteen and industrial work under fifteen: the floor the 2013 Decision keeps beside its fifteen, and not held over the later Decision. Whether either law was amended after 2002 wasn't checked. Service: not read.

sources.title: قانون رقم (45) لسنة 2002م بشأن حقوق الطفل (National Information Centre, laws database), art. 59
sources.said: مادة (59) : سن الرشد خمسة عشر سنة كاملة إذا بلغها الشخص متمتعاً بقواه العقلية رشيداً في تصرفاته يكون كامل الأهلية لمباشرة حقوقه المدنية والتصرف فيها ، ويجوز أن تشترط القوانين الخاصة سناً أعلى يحق للشخص بموجبها ممارسة حقوق أخرى أو التمتع بها ، أما البلوغ فيعمل فيه بما نصت عليه القوانين النافذة .
